question: Given $A=\begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}$, show that $A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 2\theta & -\sin 2\theta \\ \sin 2\theta & \cos 2\theta \end{bmatrix}$.
explanation:
Calculate $A^2 = A \cdot A$:

$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}$

First row, first column:

$\cos \theta \cos \theta + (-\sin \theta)\sin \theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta$

First row, second column:

$\cos \theta (-\sin \theta) + (-\sin \theta) \cos \theta = -\cos \theta \sin \theta - \sin \theta \cos \theta = -2\sin\theta \cos \theta = -\sin 2\theta$

Second row, first column:

$\sin \theta \cos \theta + \cos \theta \sin \theta = 2\sin \theta \cos \theta = \sin 2\theta$

Second row, second column:

$\sin \theta ( -\sin \theta ) + \cos \theta \cos \theta = -\sin^2 \theta + \cos^2 \theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2 \theta = \cos 2\theta$

So,

$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 2\theta & -\sin 2\theta \\ \sin 2\theta & \cos 2\theta \end{bmatrix}$.
